incidents.vector: Security breach of exchange infrastructure; technical vector not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: An estimated $5.5-6.3 billion in funds were affected in what is being called the largest crypto heist on record; roughly $1.8 billion was frozen by Tether and Circle but $1.2-3 billion remains in the attacker's control. Binance says user funds remain safe.

incidents.vector: Suspected software supply-chain compromise delivering malware ("NetamLoader") disguised as legitimate Windows update components.
incidents.impact: Malware capable of disabling security scanning, deleting logs and exfiltrating system data was found on a government Windows system running a customized OS build; full scope of compromise remains undetermined.

incidents.victim: 200+ organizations across 14+ countries (foreign ministries, defense/intelligence agencies, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, nuclear, financial and telecom sectors)
incidents.vector: Agentic AI penetration-testing framework (ARTEX, paired with the DeepSeek LLM) chaining SAML/XXE flaws, cloud metadata-service abuse, web shells and credentials recovered from leaked VPN/mail archives.
incidents.impact: Roughly 70% of targeted organizations were compromised or show evidence of likely compromise within an 11-day window, including foreign ministries, a European presidency and prime minister's office, and 19 U.S. pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, nuclear and financial-sector organizations.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack (Zawoo variant); specific vector undisclosed.
incidents.impact: An early-September attack has continued to delay clinical lab work and, as newly confirmed, coronial autopsy investigations across New Zealand.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack; specific intrusion vector undisclosed.
incidents.impact: Israel's largest car importer was hit by ransomware; the SETTRA group publicly claimed the attack this week after the incident occurred roughly two weeks earlier.

incidents.vector: Breach of an Okta single sign-on database used by DHS.
incidents.impact: Personal information on more than 41,000 DHS employees, mostly ICE and CBP staff, dating back to 2011, was leaked and re-hosted after takedown attempts.

incidents.victim: Belgian Ministry of Finance (MyMinfin tax portal)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack; specific vector undisclosed.
incidents.impact: Belgium's tax filing portal was taken offline two days before the annual filing deadline; the deadline was extended to November 16.

incidents.vector: Supply-chain compromise of third-party web-performance provider DebugBear, injecting wallet-draining code.
incidents.impact: Approximately $2.1 million in cryptocurrency was stolen from users; trading was briefly halted and Polymarket is reimbursing affected traders.

incidents.vector: Supply-chain attack: a tampered version of the Claude Code extension was distributed via the Cursor VS Code Marketplace for about 11 hours, installing a persistent SSH backdoor.
incidents.impact: Up to 5,000 developer machines were exposed to a reverse-SSH backdoor attempt and host-information exfiltration; Anthropic's own systems and the official npm/VS Code Marketplace packages were not affected.

incidents.vector: Unspecified hack.
incidents.impact: Data belonging to 2.58 million So-net customers was stolen.

incidents.vector: Breach of third-party analytics provider Amplitude.
incidents.impact: Some customer data was stolen; no funds were reported stolen.

incidents.vector: Breach of internal mobile system.
incidents.impact: No customer funds were reported stolen, according to the company.

incidents.vector: Supply-chain breach at a passenger-management supplier.
incidents.impact: Data belonging to more than 90,000 travelers was exposed.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion; specific vector undisclosed.
incidents.impact: The FEC shut down its electronic campaign-finance filing system a week before the midterm elections; the agency says the voting process itself is unaffected.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to the Onamae Desktop Cloud service hosting an FX trading platform.
incidents.impact: Attackers demanded a $50 million ransom and leaked stolen data on the dark web; GMO is offering a $1 million reward for information on the hackers.

incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center
incidents.vector: Ransomware attack; initial intrusion vector undisclosed.
incidents.impact: Ambulances were diverted and medical-school classes and outpatient surgeries were canceled; patient and employee data was stolen. No ransom was paid and systems have been fully restored.

incidents.victim: U.S. government-affiliated network (Palo Alto Networks firewalls)
incidents.vector: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/CVE-2026-109619) chained with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation exploit (CVE-2026-46300) against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: Attacker achieved root access and obtained Active Directory user/group listings, credentials, private keys and network topology within a U.S. government-affiliated environment; 24 firewalls were compromised in a broader scan, with two targeted for deep follow-on access.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion with data exfiltration, detected by government IT staff.
incidents.impact: Officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach; personal data of roughly one-third of Moldova's population was stolen.

incidents.vector: Unspecified breach.
incidents.impact: Data on all children enrolled in California's public school system over the past three years was exposed.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack; specific vector undisclosed.
incidents.impact: The hospital system operated without critical systems through a weekend and into the following Monday.

incidents.victim: eMudhra and organizations relying on its emSign G3 certificate hierarchy
incidents.vector: Cryptographically weak key generation during intermediate CA certificate issuance, allowing private-key derivation from public certificates.
incidents.impact: Eight intermediate CA keys were compromised, creating a window for TLS impersonation and traffic interception before browser and OS vendors revoked trust in the affected certificates.

incidents.victim: Multiple organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, government, manufacturing and energy sectors
incidents.vector: Exploitation of PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication-bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-0257 to bypass MFA and establish VPN access, followed by pivoting to vCenter/ESXi and offline domain-controller credential theft.
incidents.impact: Ongoing ransomware intrusions across 11 industries since June 2026; attackers disable ESXi security controls and harvest domain-wide credentials before deploying ransomware.

incidents.victim: Florida Department of Education (Student Financial Aid website)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a system or database containing applicant records.
incidents.impact: Social Security numbers and other personal information of approximately 4.9 million financial-aid applicants were exposed.

incidents.vector: Misuse of the company's member-information retrieval API.
incidents.impact: 22,519,960 customer records were exposed, including names, addresses, emails, passwords, phone numbers, dates of birth and employment information.

incidents.victim: CyberLogitec customers (40+ port authorities, maritime and shipping companies)
incidents.vector: Supply-chain compromise of maritime IT services provider CyberLogitec, pivoting into customer networks.
incidents.impact: More than 40 port authorities, maritime operators and global shipping companies were compromised and listed on a dark-web leak site; the extortion payment deadline has passed.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack; specific vector undisclosed.
incidents.impact: Disrupted services at 495 companies and local governments relying on the Japanese cloud provider.

incidents.vector: Unspecified breach by a named cybercriminal group.
incidents.impact: Stolen DMV data has continued to be offered for sale on cybercriminal forums throughout October.
